summary: Mr. Mosseri discusses when and where weddings took place based on questions following a previous discussion about the ketuba. He covers the requirement of a minion established by the Hakhamim of Halab, the former custom of midnight weddings brought from Halab, and the practices of holding weddings indoors in the Bet Kneset or formerly in the home of the father of the bride.
questions: Were weddings historically done during the day or at night?
Where did weddings take place in the old days compared to modern times?
How was the wedding ceremony conducted regarding the positioning and seating of the bride and groom?
What was the custom regarding weddings when Rabbi Jacob S. Kassen arrived in the community?
